newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold ends down but silver up on shortage.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold ends down but silver up on shortage.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 30 rupees lower at 4,700 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,730 rupees amid lower than expected seasonal buying and fresh unloading by stockists.

** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 300 rupees lower at 55,000 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,300 rupees. They were up by 100 rupees each on Saturday but were down 700 rupees each last week.

** Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees higher at 7,390 rupees per kg up against the previous close of 7,345 rupees amid shortage of ready stock and fresh industrial support. Silver was up 10 rupees per kg on Saturday but was down by 80 rupees per kg during last week.

Gold 24 carat closed 30 rupees lower at 4,700 rupees per 10 grammed against the previous close of 4,730 rupees as lower than expected seasonal buying and fresh arrivals prompted fresh selling on Tuesday, dealers said.
Gold was up 10 rupees per 10 grammes on Saturday but was down 65 rupees during last week.

Gold biscuit prices (116.50 grammes) closed 300 rupees lower at 55,000 rupees per piece after gaining 100 rupees on Saturday. The market was closed on Monday for the Hindu spring festival of colours. Gold biscuits were down 700 rupees each last week.
"Sentiment remained weak today on talk that the Indian government may liberalise gold import against special licence," said M. L. Damani, president of Bombay Bullion Exchange.

Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees higher at 7,390 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,345 rupees on the back of poor supplies and shortage of ready stock, with fresh industrial demand helping prices bounce back. Silver was up 10 rupees per kg on Saturday but was down by 80 rupees last week. (Conversion $1=35.89 rupees)
